thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: Sev2 - Shoreline (enterprise) - increased 5xxs & timeouts from apac-sin edge. Runbook 'tenant-regional-redistribute' auto-triggered. Link: https://incidents.redwood/example/2060003210

Sara_oncall: ack - i'm taking incident. collecting logs and customer context now.

Mike_sre: oncall here. checking ingress graphs and LB health.

Tina_support: customer ticket: 'we're seeing ~18% request failures, jobs stuck in queue for APAC users' — Shoreline is in a dedicated pool in apac-sin. They've flagged SLA impact.

Raj_netops: visibility: packet retransmits and high TCP RTO to our apac-sin egress range; route flaps from one transit ASN around 01:42 UTC. Looks like a peering issue.

Lucy_runtime: apac-sin worker nodes show retries to upstream services and TLS resets. eu-central and us-west pools are healthy with reserve warm capacity. We can do an edge-level weight shift or DNS diversion; DNS quicker given the customer has CNAME to our edge. We should also prime session caches to avoid cold-start latencies.

Oliver_eng: can we do an HTTP 307 redirect for active sessions instead of DNS? customer's integration expects stable host header; redirect might break some long-lived connections. DNS weighted shift safer.

Sara_oncall: plan: 1) set short TTL (20s) on Shoreline CNAME, 2) create weighted edge entries: eu-central=70, us-west=30, 3) scale eu-central pool + warm priming, 4) send customer advisory and perform canary checks.

Mike_sre: permission check: contract allows emergency traffic steering. Mai, customer consent?

Mai_custeng: customer on call - they approve emergency reroute. prefer minimal user-visible change; accept temporary latency increase.

Raj_netops: initiating DNS API call: setting TTL=20 and adding weighted records (edge: eu-central 70, us-west 30). Job id dns-7765.

incident-bot: Automation: DNS update queued.

Lucy_runtime: scaling eu-central serving: `gcloud container clusters resize shore-eu --zone=eu-central1 --num-nodes=36` and bump deployment replicas for shoreline-serving.

Sara_oncall: priming script (from eu-central bastion):

```
curl -s -H "Host: shoreline.prod.example" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANARY_TOKEN" \
  https://eu-central-proxy.internal/v1/chat -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"health-check"}],"max_tokens":2}' | jq '.status'
```

Oliver_eng: pushed small batch of synthetic sessions to warm KV caches and session prefixes. Monitor token volume and cache hit ratio.

Tina_support: customer message sent: "We've started a protective failover to EU region to mitigate packet loss impacting APAC. We'll monitor and update every 15m."

Mike_sre: canary run output: status ok, p50=180ms from eu-central, p95=560ms. No immediate 5xxs on eu path.

Raj_netops: DNS change propagated to major resolvers. Still seeing some traffic to apac-sin from legacy ISP resolvers; expected while TTL flushes.

incident-bot: Note: keep severity at Sev2. Escalate to Sev1 if customer-facing errors exceed 20% or SLA breach.

Sara_oncall: monitoring dashboards: errors in apac-sin trending down from 18% -> 6%. overall user impact decreasing.

Mike_sre: tail logs show TLS resets to apac egress resolved on some paths. Good sign. continuing to monitor.

Lucy_runtime: quality checks: ran subset of integration tests (schema + output constraints). No regressions detected. Will continue a rolling synthetic test to validate KV consistency.

Mai_custeng: customer confirms reduced failures and able to resume job processing. Thanks team.

Sara_oncall: handing to Mike for overnight monitoring at 02:55 UTC. Handoff note: watch DNS hit ratio, cache warming metrics, p95 latency for eu-central and us-west.

Mike_sre: taking over. setting alert thresholds: if error_rate > 7% or p95 > 900ms, page oncall.

Raj_netops: provider update at 03:20 UTC: peering vendor reports resolved BGP instability; suggests gradual cutback. Recommend staged return: 40% -> apac-sin for 10m, then 80% for 20m, then full 100% if green.

Sara_oncall: (handoff addendum) ensure we log 'session affinity misses' metric during cutback — look for spike in auth fails or 5xxs.

Mike_sre: initiating staged revert to apac-sin: 40% now.

```
# DNS provider API
PATCH /records/shoreline-prod {
  "weights": {"apac-sin":40, "eu-central":40, "us-west":20}
}
```

Mike_sre: 10m in - no spike. moving to 80% apac-sin.

Raj_netops: apac-sin peering stable for 50m, no packet loss alerts.

Tina_support: customer reports normal throughput.

Mike_sre: moving to 100% apac-sin, restoring TTL to 300s.

incident-bot: Automation: DNS revert recorded. Runbook step 'tenant-regional-redistribute' COMPLETE.

Lucy_runtime: scaled eu-central replicas back to baseline. Cache metrics normalized.

Sara_oncall: leaving final note: please create a short postmortem (owner: mike_sre) covering root cause, timeline, and recommendation to add automated failover playbook for dedicated tenants. Also consider adding fallback edge routes pre-provisioned for this tenant.

Mike_sre: will own postmortem. preliminary RCA: transient peering/BGP instability to apac-sin transit provider caused increased packet loss -> elevated request timeouts. Mitigation via DNS-weighted diversion to eu-central + cache priming prevented an extended outage.

Mai_custeng: scheduled customer debrief. Customer requested details on why failover was necessary and steps to reduce future occurrences.

incident-bot: Incident 2060003210 status: RESOLVED (monitoring).
